svg.aria-label: Attenuation of the trp operon: the two tandem tryptophan codons in the leader region, the route in which abundant tryptophan lets the ribosome run ahead so a terminator forms, the route in which scarce tryptophan stalls the ribosome so an antiterminator forms, and the bacterial condition that transcription and translation occur together.
svg.text: A The sensing device: a leader with two tandem Trp codons
leader region
trpE ... trpA
two Trp codons
regions 1 2 3 4 can pair in two ways
B Trp PLENTIFUL: ribosome runs on, TERMINATOR forms
ribo
charged Trp-tRNA is abundant, so the two codons are read without pause
3:4 hairpin + U run
The ribosome covers region 2, so regions 3 and 4 pair: a terminator.
RNA polymerase stops inside the leader. No enzymes are made.
C Trp SCARCE: ribosome stalls, ANTITERMINATOR forms
ribo
charged Trp-tRNA is scarce, so the ribosome waits at the Trp codons
2:3 pairing instead
The ribosome stays upstream, so regions 2 and 3 pair and the 3:4
terminator cannot form. Transcription continues into trpE.
D Why only bacteria can do this, and how it differs from repression
1 No nuclear envelope: a ribosome can translate an RNA while
polymerase is still making it.
2 A leader region carrying the two Trp codons exists.
TrpR repression vs attenuation
initiation vs elongation; senses the Trp MOLECULE vs the amount
of CHARGED tRNA; large on/off vs fine tuning. Together, ~700-fold.
Do not confuse this with eukaryotic Pol II promoter-proximal pausing. That is held by NELF and DSIF and released by P-TEFb phosphorylation —
no RNA secondary structure and no ribosome involved. Same category of "control after initiation", entirely different mechanism.
